query: What sample sizes and annotation budgets are needed for a 6–12 week pilot to estimate prevalence and achieve stable kappa for high-urgency posts given target prevalence and desired precision?

response.query: What sample sizes and annotation budgets are needed for a 6–12 week pilot to estimate prevalence and achieve stable kappa for high-urgency posts given target prevalence and desired precision?
response.answer: For a 6–12 week pilot, a sample size of 300-500 high-urgency posts and a budget for 10-20 annotators should suffice to estimate prevalence and achieve stable kappa. Larger samples improve precision.

results.title: COVID-19 Vaccination and Testing; Emergency Temporary ...
results.content: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is issuing an emergency temporary standard (ETS) to protect unvaccinated employees of large employers (100 or more employees) from the risk of contracting COVID-19 by strongly encouraging vaccination. OSHA also concludes, based on its enforcement experience during the pandemic to date, that continued reliance on existing standards and regulations, the General Duty Clause of the OSH Act, 29 U.S.C. 654(a)(1), and workplace guidance, in lieu of an ETS, is not adequate to protect unvaccinated employees from the grave danger of being infected by, and suffering death or serious health consequences from, COVID-19. For a discussion of turnover ( *i.e.* whether the ETS could affect the likelihood that an employee will remain with an employer, either because the imposition of a vaccine requirement will lead some employees to leave and find employment at an establishment not subject to the ETS, or, alternatively, to stay due to a preference for enhanced COVID-19 safety procedures), please see the cost section (Section III.d.) of this economic analysis.
